s: A company runs 120 microservices across 25 AWS accounts on Amazon ECS, Amazon EKS, AWS Lambda, and EC2 Auto Scaling groups. Several VPCs have overlapping CIDR ranges after an acquisition. Some services use AWS App Mesh, which the company must replace. Teams need HTTP and gRPC service-to-service communication, per-service authorization based on IAM principals, and request access logs. The company does not want to manage sidecar proxies, a load balancer for every service, or transit routing between VPCs. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: Move the remaining services onto App Mesh with Envoy sidecars, and connect all VPCs with a transit gateway that is shared by AWS RAM.
Expose each microservice through an internal Network Load Balancer and a VPC endpoint service, and create an interface VPC endpoint in every consumer VPC for each service that it calls.
Connect all VPCs with a transit gateway, place an internal Application Load Balancer in front of each service, and use security group rules to authorize callers.

Create an Amazon VPC Lattice service network in a central account and share it with the organization by using AWS RAM. Associate the consumer VPCs with the service network, register each microservice as a Lattice service with its compute targets, and attach auth policies that allow only SigV4-signed requests from specific IAM principals.

w.y: Amazon VPC Lattice provides managed service-to-service connectivity across accounts and VPCs (including overlapping CIDRs) for ECS, EKS, Lambda and EC2 targets, with IAM auth policies and access logs, and no sidecars or transit routing. Sharing one service network through AWS RAM is the LEAST operational overhead, and it is an AWS-recommended replacement for App Mesh.

o.A: App Mesh reached end of support on September 30, 2026, sidecars are what the company wants to avoid, and overlapping CIDRs break transit gateway routing.
o.B: Needs a load balancer per service and hundreds of endpoints, and provides no per-request IAM authorization for custom services.
o.C: Overlapping CIDRs cannot be routed, it requires a load balancer per service, and security groups cannot authorize by IAM principal.
o.D: Correct: managed L7 service networking across accounts with IAM auth policies and access logs, no sidecars or routing.
